sections.content:
10,110 people

were counted on the census as "conservation professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Conservation professionals make sure that landscapes, habitats and species are protected and enhanced using appropriate management and conservation.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "conservation professionals", 14.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "conservation professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "conservation professionals" included:

  • management consultants and business analysts
  • therapy professionals (other)
  • newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "conservation professionals" there were a similar number of men and women (51% compared with 49%).

This means "conservation professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 51% and women made up 49% of "conservation professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "conservation professionals" included:

  • chartered and certified accountants
  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • advertising accounts managers and creative directors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "conservation professionals", 11.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (77.1% compared with 22.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (83.9%) than self-employed (16.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the same region of the South West.
